thread_analysis.thread_summary: JUST.WILL Co., Ltd. (contact Hiroshi Tsukui), a new, first-time customer reached via the Allion website contact form, engages Allion (Masaya Iida, Itsuo Sakai) for Bluetooth SIG registration guidance for an Espressif ESP32-S3-based device, spanning April through September 2025. The thread documents thorough first-time-customer onboarding (registration types, cost structure), a module variant identification correction, a key distinction between chipset-level and board-level qualification (an uncertified third-party board built on a certified chipset still needing RF PHY testing), antenna documentation sourcing for an MRA-certified module, and a Compliance Folder antenna requirement satisfied via a reused prior report.
all_questions_found: What's the difference between company membership and product registration, is testing required, and can the consultant handle the entire process for an inexperienced customer? (see thread_0021_case_01)
Which ESP32-S3 module variant is being used, and is it exempt from RF/RF PHY testing and Japan radio-law certification? (see thread_0021_case_02)
Does a certified underlying chipset make an unregistered third-party board built around it exempt from RF PHY testing? (see thread_0021_case_03)
Where can antenna technical data be found for an MRA-certified module when the government database doesn't include it? (see thread_0021_case_04)
Does an antenna-integrated module exempt a product from the Compliance Folder's antenna documentation requirement? (see thread_0021_case_05)

(Administrative, not separately cased) Repeated requests for cost/process clarification, registration turnaround confirmation (3 business days after SIG payment received), and final document list confirmation -- routine onboarding administration largely already captured in the cases above.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread's most valuable technical content is case_03's distinction between chipset-level and board-level Bluetooth SIG qualification -- a customer's intuitive assumption (a certified chip makes any board built on it exempt from testing) is wrong, and the correct check is searching the SIG database for the actual board/module manufacturer's name. Case_04 and case_05 both address practical Compliance Folder document-sourcing challenges (confidential MRA antenna data; reusable manufacturer reports across unrelated projects) that recur across many customer engagements.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0021_case_01 through thread_0021_case_05 for case-specific decision logic; the throughline is verifying exact module/board identity and registration status before answering test-exemption questions, and separating the customer's various cost/responsibility axes clearly for a first-time, inexperienced customer.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; case_03 carries the highest practical risk, since incorrectly assuming an unregistered board is RF-PHY-exempt based on its chipset's QDID could lead to an incomplete registration submission.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: The consultant initially answered test-exemption questions based on the customer's generic 'ESP32-S3' reference without immediately confirming the exact variant, requiring a later correction once the customer clarified they meant the antenna-integrated WROOM-1 (not the WROOM-1U connector variant initially discussed) -- a minor but recurring pattern worth flagging for early variant confirmation in future onboarding conversations.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For first-time, inexperienced customers, proactively separate registration cost/responsibility axes early, always confirm the exact module/board variant (not just series or chipset name) before answering exemption questions, and check the SIG database for the actual board/module manufacturer's name -- not just the underlying chipset -- since chipset-level qualification does not extend to board-level RF PHY exemption for an unregistered third-party board.
